answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable security deposit before transacting — a marble-sized stake too small to matter once, but prohibitively expensive across ten thousand clones. New identities start at zero reputation and earn trust only through verifiable work, not volume. Misbehaving identities lose their deposit, so a clone farm burns capital faster than it can earn. When the tide of cheap duplicates rises, the bonded wharf holds the line: honest agents pay once, sybil swarms pay ten thousand times.
